judgment: There is trust. Great good, and no harm.
It is good to set out.
But what is there to use?
Two vessels of grain can serve for the offering.
image: A marsh under the mountain: Lessening.
So the noble one checks anger
lines: His business done, he goes quickly: no harm —
but let him weigh what to lessen.
It is good to hold firm.
He does not lessen it, but adds to it.
Someone adds to it for him:
a tortoise worth ten strings of cowries,
and it cannot be refused. Great good.
He does not lessen it, but adds to it: no harm.
It is good to set out.
He gets a servant with no household.

notes.name_en: 損 is taking away, decreasing; 'Lessening', paired with 42 Adding.
notes.judgment: 二簋 two grain vessels — a small offering when there is trust (cf. 29 L4).
notes.L5: 十朋 ten strings of cowrie money; the great tortoise shell cannot be refused (弗克違).
